## Scope

M4 separates formal properties over declared domains, statistical calibration and
closed-loop comparisons. The owner-selected scope is [OQ-22](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/decisions.qmd#oq-22). No M4 certification review
has occurred. The transport monotonicity property now has the certificates described below.

## Checked exports {#exports}

`tkit.verify.export` makes fixed float64 PyTorch copies of the Equinox networks. It includes
input transforms, normalization and physical output transforms. Transport's served response
averages members in training space before inverse signed-log; EC clamps the raw mean after
averaging. The selected pedestal retains its power-law residual, tanh-GELU, squared outputs
and density scaling, with every solution explicit.

`check_parity` rejects nonfinite arrays, shape differences and a discrepancy beyond the
selected numeric criterion. [OQ-26](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/decisions.qmd#oq-26) approves mixed relative and absolute parity after the
relative-only check exposed cancellation near zero: [13 export checks pass in each mode: all selected members, random box points, local holdouts, physical transforms and served means, with rtol=1e-12 and atol=1e-12 in each declared output unit]{.claim}[C-180](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-180){.cid .st-tested}.
Formal proofs may not bypass this gate. The artifact manifests bind model, metadata and explicit
box files and allow transport exports to load without opening the large training datasets.
They establish storage consistency, not proved physical behavior ([OQ-23](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/decisions.qmd#oq-23)).

## Property contracts {#properties}

[six property contracts load; 14 property-validation tests pass in each mode, including malformed-domain, tolerance and output-schema rejection]{.claim}[C-177](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-177){.cid .st-tested}. `tkit.verify.properties` validates model scopes, output names,
finite ordered boxes, the declared box data source, robustness tolerances and owner decisions.
The existing [OQ-20](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/decisions.qmd#oq-20) monotonicity contract is retained.

The formal engine is auto_LiRPA with the input-splitting loop described below, under [OQ-24](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/decisions.qmd#oq-24). Bounds target every member; local robustness targets the served
ensemble response. Launcher families stay categorical, and complete perturbation boxes that
leave a training domain will be reported separately. No training box is silently shrunk to
make a property pass.

## Closed-loop comparison {#closed-loop}

`tkit.verify.closed_loop` reads provenance-bound saved runs and rejects unmatched settings,
time/radial grids, nonfinite profiles or unconverged solver records. It checks that a face
served by the surrogate was served by TGLF in the reference.

The historical paper eq. 41 convention is retained:

$$ E = 100\frac{\sqrt{\operatorname{mean}((T_{sur}-T_{ref})^2)}}
                    {\operatorname{mean}(T_{sur})}. $$

The guard is defined on faces, while temperatures are cell-centred. Both temperatures are
linearly interpolated to the same served faces. Whole-profile errors and a supplementary
comparison using cells with both adjacent faces served remain visible. The saved runs' grids
are uniform; the reader rejects other grids without explicit face coordinates.

ITER passes ([served-face T_e 7.42%, T_i 8.18%, both passing the 15% limit; whole profile 7.72/9.23%; 34 of 51 final-state faces served]{.claim}[C-178](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-178){.cid .st-measured}). MAST-U fails ([served-face T_e 35.33%, T_i 49.15%, both failing 15%; whole profile 41.51/62.39%; cells with both adjacent faces served give 11.86/23.24%, still failing T_i; 13 of 26 final-state faces served]{.claim}[C-179](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-179){.cid .st-measured}), with the conservative
cell diagnostic also failing ion temperature. Its failure remains ceiling [K-030](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/ceilings.qmd#k-030). The mask
is only the final accepted state's guard diagnostic; it does not measure fallback calls
throughout the trajectory.

### MAST-U scope (OQ-42) {#mastu-scope}

*Decided 25 Oct 2026.* The MAST-U comparison against a TGLF reference trajectory (remediation
step R6) is recorded as not evaluable, and MAST-U is presented for certification review with that
limitation stated, alongside [K-030](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/ceilings.qmd#k-030) and [K-032](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/ceilings.qmd#k-032). ITER's pass stands. The model, guard,
acceptance limits and frozen splits are unchanged, and no further MAST-U reference compute is
planned ([entry 70](../log/70-owner-limits-the-mastu-certification-scope.qmd)).

The evidence is a read-only screen (`scripts/m4_mastu_projection_screen.py`) of [OQ-38](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/decisions.qmd#oq-38)'s
projection rule: in the reference only, set each negative raw TGLF heat diffusivity to zero,
log it, and stop if a projected heat-flux magnitude reaches 1 gB. The single approved
projected run stopped on that rule and saved no trajectory. The screen applies the rule to
every interior face of the 40 saved states of the unprojected reference run (same profiles),
inverting TORAX's conversion to obtain the signed fluxes:

| quantity | result |
|---|---|
| negative raw heat diffusivities, and those reaching the stop | [150 negative raw heat diffusivities at 19 faces; 46 would reach the 1 gB stop, at 31 of 40 states, the first at state 1]{.claim}[C-240](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-240){.cid .st-measured} |
| of those, on faces the projected reference would serve | [26 would be served, the first at state 4 (faces 11 and 12, ion, −8.0 and −33.8 gB); near the axis the projected magnitude reaches 6020 gB]{.claim}[C-241](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-241){.cid .st-measured} |
| candidate against the guarded historical reference, shared TGLF faces | [T_e 32.0%, T_i 41.5% on the 14 faces where both serve TGLF, against the 15% limit]{.claim}[C-242](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-242){.cid .st-measured} |

The stop applies to every projection, served or not, so on this trajectory it fires at
state 1; served faces alone would stop it at state 4. Projection would also change
which faces are served: 840 of the 1040 face-states against 717 historically. Limits: the
fluxes are inferred, not direct TGLF outputs; a projected run diverges from the saved
trajectory after its first served projection, so the screen is not a replay; the edge faces
0 and 25 have no interior inversion.
The last row compares with the guarded TGLF/fallback hybrid and is descriptive, not a gate
result.

## MAST-U remediation diagnosis {#mastu-remediation}

The owner prioritizes the failed MAST-U criterion ([OQ-25](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/decisions.qmd#oq-25)). Matched final-state probes
show substantial flux error: [all 17 in-domain final-state probes succeed; on 12 served faces with reference flux above 1 gB, median relative errors are 41.17% Q_e and 74.27% Q_i; an unconstrained v3 control gives 38.05/71.88%]{.claim}[C-181](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-181){.cid .st-measured}. The existing unconstrained v3 model
also misses those feedback states. That control is diagnostic and does not meet the
owner's monotonicity contract; pointwise scores are not a coupled comparison.

The accepted-state replay reproduces the failed saved trajectory: [all saved temperature, density and psi values are reproduced exactly; four final inner faces exceed the existing ion-diffusivity guard bound; 44.81% of accepted-state face diagnostics reject the surrogate]{.claim}[C-182](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-182){.cid .st-measured}.
Four final inner faces lie in the model's box but exceed the ion-diffusivity guard
bound. Captured masks cover accepted states, not the solver's intermediate evaluations.
The isolated inner served face has zero final heat flux in both model and TGLF even
though its temperature differs. No face is removed from the acceptance comparison.

The approved refresh collected feedback-state labels on training equilibria only, with
both test equilibria excluded. It retains full solver inputs and applies the approved-region
filter. The local result review checks the finished artifacts: [eight local checks pass for approved allocation/time, hashes and lineage, full-input alignment, case budget, unique coordinates, training-only equilibria, source model and finite successful labels]{.claim}[C-183](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-183){.cid .st-measured}.
It compares each label input row with the selected case and the source trajectory's
accepted-state solver arrays, and binds lineage by hash. These checks establish collection
integrity; they do not establish held-out accuracy or a successful coupled remedy.
The owner approved artifact synchronization in [OQ-28](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/decisions.qmd#oq-28). We checked remote privacy settings
and downloaded every uploaded record by artifact identifier: [all 26 uploaded artifact records covering 18 distinct files match both remote SHA-256 metadata and downloaded bytes; the folder and private visibility match the approved request, and the offline payload queue is empty]{.claim}[C-184](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-184){.cid .st-measured}.
Duplicate provenance sidecars are retained as distinct records; name-based retrieval is
ambiguous for those duplicates. Downloads by identifier verify every record without
changing the remote artifacts. Retraining and an improved closed-loop
result remain pending. No new certificate or domain is deployed, and the 15% tolerance is unchanged.

Formal certificates, conformal coverage, the EC coupled reference check, certificate-bound

The owner prioritizes diagnosing and remediating the MAST-U closed-loop failure first ([OQ-25](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/decisions.qmd#oq-25)).

## Candidate replay preparation {#candidate-replay-preparation}

[Entry 48](../log/48-mastu-candidate-replay-preparation.qmd) records R6 tooling.
The runner supports an explicit immutable candidate directory while preserving default
model selection. New trajectories record the full scenario configuration, source runner,
model and metadata, scenario plan and equilibrium provenance. Preparation binds a source
snapshot and checks every external input digest and environment version before execution.

Reference reuse reconstructs the historical scenario from its checksum-bound runner and
clean source revision. Physics/core/dataset modules and the scenario plan are byte-identical
to that revision. Solver, fallback, wrapper post-processing and guard settings match recorded
metadata; the candidate differs in its model path. Its previously audited box stays fixed.
Historical metadata lacks the run index, but its bound runner selects the first scenario
explicitly. External dependency bytes and a full resolved configuration were not recorded
historically; the audit states that limitation and checks pinned/current versions instead
of supplying retrospective hashes. Actual post-run configuration, grids, time points,
provenance and finite convergence remain required.

The formal comparison uses every candidate-served face, interpolating both profiles onto
those coordinates and normalizing RMS difference by the candidate temperature mean. The
report retains original served-mask counts, overlap and faces added/removed. A separate
fixed-baseline-mask diagnostic evaluates the candidate temperatures on the old faces;
it never replaces the formal mask. Whole-profile and both-adjacent-faces cell errors are
retained. An isolated served face remains eligible for the formal metric even when the
supplementary cell metric is unavailable. Existing comparison defaults are preserved.

Accepted-state history captures generic guard features and raw coefficients before
post-processing. Rejection diagnostics count model-domain violations, generic feature
finiteness/box failures, nonfinite coefficients, negative diffusivities, excessive
diffusivity and convection. Predicate counts overlap, so a separate priority partition
provides counts that sum to the number of rejected face states. Candidate diagnostics
must reproduce the saved raw predicate exactly. The historical replay lacks generic
features; its unavailable predicate evidence stays explicit. These rates describe accepted
states, not intermediate transport calls, and no fallback acceptance threshold is chosen.

[40 focused checks pass in normal and Tier A modes; the two-step training-only candidate smoke is finite and reconstructs the raw accepted-state guard predicate exactly]{.claim}[C-188](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-188){.cid .st-tested} checks configuration/mask isolation, raw guard accounting, immutable
package/input rejection and historical runner compatibility. A bounded two-step smoke uses
a training equilibrium only and validates source-package execution, finite profiles and
raw guard reconstruction. Saved baseline artifacts also reproduce the existing comparison
exactly through the new report. No held-out candidate result or formal certificate is claimed.

## Signed heat conversion review {#signed-heat-conversion-review}

The saved-state review reconstructs face temperatures and radial derivatives
with the pinned transport solver's cell representation and bound magnetic
geometry. Source checks cover the recorded conversion, geometry and gradient
files. No simulation or transport model is prepared; physical solver calls are
forbidden. Every state of the investigated face is retained.

For each heat channel the converter uses

\[
P_s=Q_s^{gB}Q_{GB}\,V'/\rho_b,\qquad
\chi_s=-P_s/(n_s\partial_{\rho_n}T_s\,g_1/V'+\epsilon),
\]

with temperature in joules and the fixed numerical denominator correction.
Inverting this equation gives an inferred heat flux, which is converted back
through the native implementation. [33 focused checks pass in each mode, including 14 new sign/units/history tests; all 80 native heat-converter round trips meet the mixed 1e-12 parity criterion (maximum absolute difference 8.88e-16 m²/s), 32 numerical source files match the diagnostic bindings, and all 78 source modules pass typing]{.claim}[C-196](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-196){.cid .st-tested} records those numerical
checks and synthetic tests. A round trip checks algebra and units; it cannot
independently validate the originating solver flux.

[the final electron heat flux is inferred as -0.001689376033 gB; all 9 negative channel records at 8 accepted states have outward-decreasing temperature and no denominator-epsilon sign reversal, with maximum epsilon ratio 1.03e-11; all negative magnitudes are below 1 gB]{.claim}[C-195](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-195){.cid .st-measured} narrows the sign diagnosis. Temperatures decrease outward
in all negative heat-channel records, and the denominator correction changes
none of their signs. The saved coefficients therefore imply inward signed heat
flux in this representation. Their magnitudes are below the offline accuracy
gate's reference-flux floor; neither that gate nor their small size establishes
physical validity or a numerical-error explanation. The inferred ion channel
is the reference worker's sum over main and impurity ions, whereas the surrogate
learns main-ion heat flux. Separate species contributions remain unobserved.

The current raw guard rejects negative diffusivity before post-processing.
Moving a positive floor before that rejection changes reference physics and
coverage. A signed-flux-preserving closure would require an explicit stable
representation and compatible surrogate contract; it cannot be inferred from
one effective coefficient. The current in-memory interface does not expose
mode spectra, so richer collection requires another prepared output route.

This is an algebraic/source review, not an adopted physical remedy. [OQ-32](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/decisions.qmd#oq-32) now
selects retaining the current nonnegative contract while investigating. Formal
candidate acceptance remains not evaluable, and [K-030](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/ceilings.qmd#k-030) stays open. Current model/guard, every face, splits and
tolerances are preserved. Entry 52 is the narrative account.

## Direct heat diagnostic route {#direct-heat-diagnostic-route}

An original native driver links the byte-bound TGLF library, reads the complete
generated input and executes one local-state solve. Full-precision text retains
particle and heat flux by species, low-k heat totals, the native ky grid and
weights, growth/frequency pairs, and saturated and quasilinear heat spectra by
species, field, ky and mode. An independent synthetic branch fills those arrays
without reading an equilibrium or calling the solver. The strict reader rejects
missing, extra, nonfinite or dimensionally inconsistent records.

The paired route runs the pinned in-memory wrapper in a fresh process with the
same complete defaults, global settings and prepared local inputs. Input precedence
matches the reference worker. Native shape parameter names omit the wrapper's
local suffix; mapping them preserves register values and the native generated-file
audit checks all settings. No parser default silently replaces a declared value.

For the declared logarithmic ky grid, each interval uses
`D = log(k1/k0)/(k1-k0)`, `w1 = k1*(1-k0*D)` and
`w0 = k0*(k1*D-1)`, with first weights zero and the first ky. The contribution
is `w0*previous_spectrum + w1*current_spectrum`. Sum all fields, modes and
intervals for total heat; native low-k heat retains phi and perpendicular
magnetic fields through ky at most one. Keep all signed contributions and
compare totals at mixed relative/absolute tolerance 1e-12 in gyro-Bohm units.

Separate comparisons report native versus paired species fluxes, and paired
electron/total-ion flux versus the saved inverse conversion. Any disagreement
is retained as diagnostic evidence. The native sheared double-pass eigenvalues
may retain unsheared first-pass values; growth/frequency pairs alone neither
label a mode physically nor prove numerical convergence. Solver status and
finite output checks supply only the supported numerical diagnostics.

[55 focused checks pass in each mode, including 22 direct-output and settings checks; all 79 source modules pass typing; the compiled synthetic writer preserves signed species heat and passes total/low-k spectral parity without calling TGLF]{.claim}[C-197](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-197){.cid .st-tested} records preparation checks. This does not establish direct
physical flux parity, reference admissibility or coupled acceptance. [OQ-33](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/decisions.qmd#oq-33)'s
permission for runs shorter than six hours leaves the selected model/guard,
physical contract, training isolation and owner physics decisions in force.

## Diagnostic wrapper status fix {#diagnostic-wrapper-status-fix}

The first rich diagnostic failed in paired reporting after its first solve:
the compiled wrapper exposes integrated flux registers but not the Fortran
interface's error-status register. Source availability is insufficient evidence
of Python-interface availability. The consumed attempt retains partial native
output, failed logs, executed-call count and final scheduler accounting.

Paired reporting now records whether status is exposed, preserves absent status
as unavailable, validates finite fluxes and retains any reported failure status.
Native status remains available through the driver. This checks software/output
integrity; unavailable convergence evidence is not replaced by a zero status.
[25 diagnostic checks pass in each mode, including unavailable status, exposed failure status and nonfinite output; 33 unchanged focused checks are retained for 58 focused recorded passes per mode]{.claim}[C-198](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-198){.cid .st-tested} binds the synthetic worker regressions. A new package is frozen
after the correction, with a separate summary and retained test-report directory;
consumed request evidence is never overwritten.
## Signed reference literature review {#signed-reference-literature-review}

The complete local-state collection is retained despite a subsequent tracking
failure ([648 integrity checks pass on the complete 15-state collection; all affected signed states agree between backends, but four control states fail the existing parity criterion; original terminal tracking failure is preserved and archive recovery calls no solver]{.claim}[C-199](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-199){.cid .st-measured}). The offline tracker copied repeated basenames;
archival recovery instead preserves relative case paths in one checksum-bound
bundle. Recovery does not call the solver or alter original accounting.

The owner delegates approval of the recommended reference method ([OQ-34](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/decisions.qmd#oq-34)).
The target is signed, species-resolved TGLF with fixed turbulence settings and
matched geometry, normalization and transport equations. The present guarded
hybrid trajectory remains a regression baseline with unresolved coverage.
Numerical reproducibility, physical validation and coupled acceptance are distinct.

[GACODE output definitions](https://gacode.io/tglf/tglf_output_list.html) distinguish
species energy weights, eigenvalues and integrated spectra.
[Staebler et al. (2024), §5.2](https://doi.org/10.1088/1741-4326/ad6ba5) motivates
checking anomalous reduced-model cases before higher-fidelity gyrokinetic study.
[Snoep et al. (2025)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.03459) demonstrates matched
spectral and heat-flux verification. [Lestz et al. (2025)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.04359)
shows spherical-tokamak predictions depend on turbulence and transport treatment.
These sources support the verification method, not this case's physical validity.

Repeatability tooling retains two fresh-process results per selected state and
backend, each compared with its consumed output at the existing mixed 1e-12
criterion ([31 synthetic diagnostic tests pass in each mode, including archive identity and repeatability completeness/discrepancy checks; 33 unchanged focused records are retained, giving 64 focused recorded passes per mode]{.claim}[C-200](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-200){.cid .st-tested}). Missing identities or nonfinite values invalidate
the collection. No averaging, favorable-backend selection, negative-flux clipping
or physical mode assignment is performed. A flux-preserving conservative stable
energy closure remains to be reviewed; a negative effective turbulent diffusivity
does not by itself justify negative total diffusion.
## Reference repeatability {#reference-repeatability}

## Transport monotonicity {#transport-monotonicity}

The V4 result is [all 20 members of each ensemble pass both heat-flux monotonicity properties, with derivative lower bound zero over the full training box]{.claim}[C-247](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-247){.cid .st-measured}. Narrative entry 74 accompanies this
technical account. The result proves an imposed network
property, with the [K-025](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/ceilings.qmd#k-025) physical-model departure caveat retained.

For one constrained head, write its derivative as

$$
\frac{\partial Q}{\partial g}
= \frac{s_y}{s_x} W_{out} D_L W_L \cdots D_0 w_g.
$$

The gradient coordinate is excluded from the free trunk and from its own head's free
input vector. The effective constrained weights are absolute values of saved parameters;
all normalization scales are positive. For ELU, the derivative is $\exp(\min(z,0))$;
for reflected ELU it is $\exp(\min(-z,0))$; for the saturated mix it is
$\exp(-\max(|z|-1,0))$. Every derivative lies in $[0,1]$.

The structural route checks the saved routing, finite parameters, scales and supported
transforms. The second route exports the derivative product itself and uses
[auto_LiRPA interval bound propagation](https://github.com/Verified-Intelligence/auto_LiRPA)
over independent diagonal entries in $[0,1]$. This enlarged slope domain contains the
image of the entire raw-input box; no box shrinking or input split is required. The
result is a non-negative derivative before the output ReLU. The positive affine maps,
ReLU, inverse signed-log transform and mean preserve monotonicity through serving.

Each export and derivative graph is checked against JAX before the corresponding proof,
on random-box and original held-out points, under [OQ-26](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/decisions.qmd#oq-26). These numerical comparisons
validate the implementation path; the domain-wide result comes from the structural and
interval arguments. The certificates cover real-valued functions represented by the
saved parameters, not directed-rounding guarantees for every floating-point execution.

Certificates retain individual member/pair bounds, model and box hashes, verifier versions
and source digests. V4 is complete for the two baseline transport ensembles. Physical
reference admissibility, output bounds, conformal calibration, production guard binding,
CI re-proofs and the final certification review remain separate obligations.

## Output bounds {#output-bounds}

The first bounded run is audited: EC [all five EC members have finite CROWN bounds for both launcher families; current and width bounds remain very loose]{.claim}[C-262](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-262){.cid .st-measured}; pedestal [all nine pedestal pressure and half-width pairs have finite bounds over the recorded ITER trajectory box, with the widening and domain clipping stated]{.claim}[C-263](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-263){.cid .st-measured}.
Transport remains unresolved ([all twenty members of each transport ensemble have finite training-space bounds that overflow the inverse signed-log transform; no finite physical guard domain is certified]{.claim}[C-264](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-264){.cid .st-measured}). V5 is not complete and these bounds
are not installed in production guards. Narrative entry 78 accompanies this record.

V5 now has an executable CROWN calculation and complete input splitting. The verifier
first checks each proof export against JAX on random box points and the original held-out
inputs. Transport's input logarithms map interval endpoints monotonically. Its signed-log
inverse is applied only after bounding the training-space output. EC fixes the launcher
indicator to one family at a time while retaining every other stored input range, then
applies the serving clamps to each member's interval.

The proof graph expresses ELU as

$$\operatorname{ELU}(x)=\operatorname{ReLU}(x)
  +\exp(-\operatorname{ReLU}(-x))-1.$$

The saturated monotone-head activation uses the equivalent expression

$$\operatorname{clip}(x,-1,1)
 +\exp(-\operatorname{ReLU}(-x-1))
 -\exp(-\operatorname{ReLU}(x-1)).$$

These identities avoid unsupported export operators. They preserve the real-valued
function, but the separate relaxations can be loose; passing parity does not guarantee
useful bounds. The retained certificate names the float64 calculation and does not claim
directed-rounding verification of IEEE execution.

Each split bisects the largest side relative to the original box. A parent is replaced
only after both children have bounds. Child intervals are intersected with their parent,
and the final interval is the minimum lower and maximum upper bound across all retained
leaves. The leaf and time budgets are explicit. The time budget is checked between bound
calls; the execution wrapper supplies the hard process limit. Sampled extrema measure the
interval's tightness and must lie inside it; samples never supply the proof.

For the pedestal, the diagnostic now saves the upstream input vector at every retained
output state, its feature names and model hash. The proof box encloses those vectors,
widened by a declared fraction of the upstream range on each axis. Any clipping of that
margin at the upstream domain is recorded; a visited point outside the upstream domain
fails. The upstream box alone cannot replace a missing trajectory. CROWN bounds the
neural residual; interval composition adds the power law, squares each solution and
multiplies each pressure by the positive density interval. All pressure and half-width
solutions remain explicit, including the GH solution used by TORAX.

Reports bind the model, property, boxes, datasets, producing source and verifier library.
A nonfinite physical interval is recorded as unknown. Such a row supplies no guard domain;
V10 integration requires usable certified bounds and the owner's fallback-rate threshold.

### Optimized output bounds {#optimized-output-bounds}

The runner also supports `--method alpha-CROWN`, with explicit optimizer iteration and
soft time budgets. Ordinary CROWN remains the default. On every sub-box, the optimized
route computes ordinary CROWN, interval propagation and alpha-CROWN, then intersects
their output intervals. Thus it cannot loosen the same sub-box's baseline bound, and
interval propagation retains structural ranges such as nonnegative heat-flux outputs.
Invalid or nonfinite optimizer results fail explicitly.

The optimizer budget applies separately to lower and upper bound calculations and is
checked between iterations. Graph setup and an in-progress iteration can exceed it;
a separate process timeout supplies the hard limit. Certificates and their provenance
record the selected method, iteration cap and soft time budget. Arithmetic remains
float64 throughout. A physical-transform overflow now identifies inverse signed-log and
the largest training-bound magnitude in the retained failure reason.

The retained follow-up uses the original complete transport boxes and weights. Its
settings are [three optimizer iterations, a five-second soft budget per bound side and one leaf per member; both twenty-member runs finished within the nine-minute hard process limit]{.claim}[C-267](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-267){.cid .st-measured}. The widths relative to the earlier run are
[median width 0.164 of the earlier bound, range 0.082–0.605 across member outputs; all twenty physical member results remain unknown]{.claim}[C-265](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-265){.cid .st-measured} for ITER and [median width 0.114 of the earlier bound, range 0.060–0.220 across member outputs; all twenty physical member results remain unknown]{.claim}[C-266](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-266){.cid .st-measured} for MAST-U. This compares one-leaf
optimized bounds with four-leaf ordinary CROWN bounds; it is not an experiment that
holds the partition budget fixed. Every physical member result remains unknown.
No production guard domain follows from this experiment.

For intervals $[l_C,u_C]$, $[l_I,u_I]$ and $[l_A,u_A]$ enclosing the same output,
the returned interval is

$$[\max(l_C,l_I,l_A),\;\min(u_C,u_I,u_A)].$$

This cannot loosen the ordinary CROWN interval on that same sub-box. Nonfinite or
inconsistent intervals are rejected. The retained audit checks model and property
identity against the earlier run, frozen source digests, complete input coverage,
all member outcomes and the physical-transform overflow reasons. This audit shares
the toolkit's provenance machinery; it does not supply independent verification of
auto_LiRPA or directed-rounding guarantees.

The implementation is retained in the experiment's frozen source snapshot and
was integrated in the subsequent proof-tool commit after focused validation.

## Conformal calibration {#conformal}

V7 is complete for the three labelled surrogates ([90% intervals calibrated on the v1 validation split cover 0.887–0.907 on the v1 test and v2-random splits (6 outputs, ITER and MAST-U); 9 of 12 lie in the 0.893–0.907 range expected for exchangeable data, the other three miss it by at most 0.006]{.claim}[C-256](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-256){.cid .st-measured},
[the same intervals cover 0.996–1.000 of the v3 test states; there the half-width that would give 90% is 3.3–5.5 times smaller in signed-log units (ITER Q_e 0.48 against 2.21)]{.claim}[C-257](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-257){.cid .st-measured}, [90% intervals calibrated on 190 guard-accepted validation states (4 runs) cover 0.876–0.978 of 548 served test states (8 runs); all six outputs lie within or above the 0.856–0.938 range expected for exchangeable data; per-run coverage 0.78–1.00]{.claim}[C-258](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-258){.cid .st-measured}). Entry 76 is the narrative account.

For each served output, with prediction $\hat y$ and label $y$ on $n$ calibration points,
the score is $s_i = |y_i - \hat y_i|$. The half-width is the $k$-th smallest score, with
$k = \lceil (n+1)(1-\alpha) \rceil$ and $\alpha = 0.1$. The interval is
$[\hat y - q, \hat y + q]$. If calibration and test points are exchangeable, the interval
covers a new label with probability at least $1-\alpha$. The probability is marginal,
over both the calibration draw and the new point. MAPIE's prefit `SplitConformalRegressor`
computes $q$, and the code checks each value against the exact rank.

The prediction is the one each guard serves.
- **Transport.** The prediction is the members' mean in training space,
  $t = \operatorname{sign}(Q)\log(1 + |Q|)$. The score is taken in $t$, and the physical
  interval is the inverse transform of $[\hat t - q, \hat t + q]$. The transform is
  increasing, so coverage is the same in both spaces. A half-width $q$ spans a factor
  $e^{q}$ on $1 + |Q|$.
- **EC.** The prediction is the bounded per-MW output. Only states that the EC source's
  guard would accept count: padded box, finite outputs, and member spreads within the
  source defaults. Transport counts only points inside its training box.

Calibration uses the split recorded with each model, which also chose each member's
early-stopping epoch. Test coverage is the evidence. For $m$ test points, the number
covered under exchangeability is beta-binomial with parameters $(m, k, n+1-k)$. Its central
90% range, which includes both random draws, is stored beside each coverage. Before
calibrating, the code re-scores every split and must match the model's stored RMSE to
$10^{-4}$; the match was exact.

The results, stored per surrogate:
- **Transport, data drawn like the calibration split.** Coverage is close to 0.9.
- **Transport, held-out TORAX trajectory states.** Coverage is 0.996–1.000. The half-widths
  that would give 90% there are 3.3–5.5 times smaller. Whether to add a loop-state
  calibration for M5 awaits an owner decision.
- **Transport, by flux size.** The score is uniform in $t$, so coverage is lower where
  $|Q| > 1$ gB (0.86–0.90 on v1 test) and higher below it.
- **EC.** Pooled coverage of the 548 served states from eight held-out runs is 0.876–0.978.
  Per run it ranges from 0.78 to 1.00. Within a run, states are correlated.
- **Pedestal.** EPEDNN has no labelled data here, so it has no interval.

Records bind the model and manifest hashes through provenance sidecars. Readers obtain
them through `load_record`, which refuses a record whose model hash differs.

### Loop-state calibration (OQ-44) {#conformal-loop}

The owner chose a second transport calibration on the states the coupled runs visit, for
M5 ([calibrated on half of the held-out v3 trajectory runs, the 90% half-widths are 0.21–0.32 of the V7 values; the intervals span a factor 1.8–3.3 on 1 + abs(flux) instead of 9–60]{.claim}[C-259](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-259){.cid .st-measured}, [calibrated on 16 held-out runs and tested on the other 16, coverage is 0.870–0.894; the reverse direction gives 0.905–0.924; single runs 0.75–0.97]{.claim}[C-260](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-260){.cid .st-measured}, [calibrated on 4 held-out runs, the intervals cover 0.936–0.966 of the other 4; calibrated the other way they cover 0.711–0.818; not reliable for a new ITER run]{.claim}[C-261](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-261){.cid .st-measured}). Entry 77 is the
narrative account. The V7 records above remain the M4 deliverable.

The held-out v3 test runs are whole TORAX trajectories: eight for ITER and 32 for MAST-U.
The split rule was committed before any residual on these states was computed:
- group the runs by scenario family (ITER) or equilibrium (MAST-U);
- permute each group's runs with a fixed seed;
- deal the runs alternately to half A (calibration) and half B (report);
- drop states shared by runs in both halves (common start-up states).

The method is otherwise the V7 one. The reverse direction, calibrating on B and reporting
on A, tests whether runs are exchangeable.

The half-widths fall to 0.21–0.32 of the box-wide values. For MAST-U, coverage of the other
half is 0.870–0.894, and 0.905–0.924 in reverse; single runs range from 0.75 to 0.97. For
ITER, coverage of B is 0.936–0.966, but only 0.711–0.818 in reverse. The marginal
guarantee assumes that calibration and test points are exchangeable. With four runs per
half and systematic differences between runs, that assumption fails for ITER. A
calibration that treats runs as the unit needs more held-out trajectories than the eight
available.

### Direct ELU pilot {#direct-elu-pilot}

A separate proof graph replaces the ELU decomposition with a direct convex
relaxation. For alpha=1, let $f(x)=x$ for $x\ge0$ and $f(x)=e^x-1$ otherwise.
On a finite interval $[l,u]$, the tangent at $t$ gives
$f(x)\ge f(t)+f'(t)(x-t)$, and convexity gives
$f(x)\le f(l)+(f(u)-f(l))(x-l)/(u-l)$. Point intervals use the local derivative;
positive intervals are exactly linear. The fixed tangent uses the interval midpoint
clipped to $[-1,0]$, with exact handling for point and positive intervals. This
choice is valid but does not optimize tightness.

The saturated head has the equivalent expression
$f(1-\operatorname{ReLU}(-s))-f(1-\operatorname{ReLU}(s))$.
Each term is in $[-1,1]$, so the expression retains the structural range $[-2,2]$
without subtracting unbounded linear terms. Input preprocessing, normalization,
weights, heat-output ReLU and inverse signed-log remain those of the saved model.
The direct-ELU operator is used only by the separate experimental proof runner.

Fresh JAX parity on random-box and original held-out points precedes each proof,
including the existing physical-export check. CROWN is intersected with interval
propagation. The focused checks are [40 focused checks pass in both normal and Tier A modes; lint, formatting and typing pass]{.claim}[C-269](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-269){.cid .st-measured}. The pilot outcome is
[member 0 of each ensemble remains unknown; both processes complete in about 23 seconds, with physical inverse-transform overflow and looser intervals than the earlier optimized run]{.claim}[C-268](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-268){.cid .st-measured}: both selected members remain unknown, and the unoptimized
bounds are looser than the previous optimized calculation. The other members were
not attempted. No physical counterexample or new guard domain follows.

The audit binds saved source, model, property, full-box intervals and process
outcomes. Arithmetic has the same float64 real-network scope as the earlier V5
calculations. Improve intermediate intervals and tangent selection before another
frozen pilot; a larger run of the current method is not justified by these results.

### Optimized direct ELU and intermediate diagnostics {#optimized-direct-elu}

The direct-ELU lower relaxation can be parameterized by slope rather than tangent
location. For $a\in[0,1]$,

$$f(x)\ge ax+a-1-a\log a.$$

For $a>0$ this is the tangent at $\log a$; at $a=0$ its continuous limit is the
constant $-1$. This includes strongly saturated lower bounds that the earlier
fixed tangent, clipped to $[-1,0]$, could not select. Optimizer parameters are
clipped to $[0,1]$ separately per objective and bound side. Positive-only and
point intervals retain their exact affine expression. The upper secant and the
saved network remain unchanged. A finite logarithm floor handles the zero-slope
limit with a conservative intercept and finite gradients.

The runner computes CROWN and interval propagation first, then alpha-CROWN, and
intersects all three results. It saves each interval separately so the effect
of optimization can be assessed on the same graph and domain. It also records
the minimum lower endpoint, maximum upper endpoint, largest neuron width and
sign-region counts for each ELU input in the baseline CROWN pass. Completed
diagnostics remain available if subsequent optimization fails.

The new frozen pilot uses member 0 of each baseline ensemble, a single leaf and
twelve optimizer iterations with a ten-second soft budget per bound side. Each
process finishes in about 45 seconds. Its outcome is [both selected members remain unknown despite interval-width reductions of about 30–275 times against the same-graph fixed-tangent baseline; physical inverse-transform overflow persists]{.claim}[C-272](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-272){.cid .st-measured}; its
validation is [50 focused checks pass normally and with Tier B disabled; repository lint, formatting and typing of all 91 source modules pass]{.claim}[C-273](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-273){.cid .st-measured}. The training-space interval widths are
0.00364–0.02586 of the same-process unoptimized widths for ITER and
0.00549–0.03332 for MAST-U. No finite physical enclosure results.

There are 39 direct-ELU nodes in each graph. Baseline activation-input widths
reach $1.1014\times10^{10}$ for ITER and $1.1079\times10^9$ for MAST-U. These
intervals describe a relaxation and need not be reachable model activations.
The retained source/model/property hashes and saved-output audit preserve the
comparison. Next tighten intermediate intervals, using analytic activation
ranges while retaining complete input coverage, before another member-level
pilot. The present result does not justify an ensemble expansion or a guard
output domain. V5 and [K-033](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/ceilings.qmd#k-033) remain open.

The two-member full-box pilot gives [both selected transport members remain physically unknown; largest baseline activation widths fall to 0.246 and 0.449 of the preceding pilot, but inverse signed-log overflow persists]{.claim}[C-274](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-274){.cid .st-measured}. activation-input widths fall to 0.2456 of the preceding ITER width and 0.4491

### EC local robustness and recorded states {#ec-local-robustness}

The EC robustness property applies to the served ensemble heating centre. If
$g_i(x)$ is member $i$'s raw output in physical units, the source returns

$$c(x)=\operatorname{clip}\left(\frac{1}{M}\sum_i g_i(x)_2,0,1\right).$$

The proof graph sums raw member centres and divides by the member count. This
preserves the batch axis for the verifier. A monotone clamp is applied to the
final raw enclosure. Clamping each member first would change the response.
Fresh parity against JAX is checked on recorded states and original held-out
inputs before any local bound can be issued.

The exact input matrix is recorded from TORAX's accepted output states using
the source's own interpolation: electron temperature, density and effective
charge at the reference tabular radii, then the launcher flag and launch
coordinates. Saved face profiles allow an independent reconstruction. Model
and metadata hashes, complete input and resolved configurations, times,
numerical outputs and raw guard decisions accompany the trace. The result is
[30 upper-launcher states (29 served) and 27 equatorial-launcher states (16 served) retain exact features, profiles, outputs, model identity, configurations and guard decisions]{.claim}[C-275](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-275){.cid .st-measured}. This is state recording, not a new physical reference pass.

At a state $x$, continuous coordinates receive half-width
$\delta_j=0.01(u_j-l_j)$ from the full stored training ranges; the launcher flag
has zero half-width. The full local box is $[x-\delta,x+\delta]$. The property
requires it to lie inside $[l,u]$; boundary sides are not clipped. Only an
eligible box can be certified against $|c(z)-c(x)|\le0.05$ throughout the box.
A true evaluated violating point can falsify the property. An enclosure that
extends past the tolerance is unknown unless such a point is found.

Every recorded box is out of domain ([all 57 complete EC local boxes are out of domain, including all 45 served states; zero robustness proofs or model counterexamples are claimed]{.claim}[C-276](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-276){.cid .st-measured}). Effective charge
lies near the lower 1.6 boundary and its symmetric perturbation extends to
about 1.596. Upper and equatorial launcher positions occupy opposite training
R/Z edges; perturbing either position symmetrically crosses a boundary at every
state. Some late equatorial temperature profiles are outside the trained range
as well. The state guard can serve a point at an edge without certifying a
neighbourhood. No CROWN state-bound calculation is needed for these exclusions.

[K-034](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/ceilings.qmd#k-034) records this limitation. Under [OQ-45](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/decisions.qmd#oq-45) the owner selected retaining the strict
result as a limitation, with no clipped box or changed perturbation scope. No
property or tolerance has changed. The deterministic later reference selection is [twenty output states per launcher are selected at evenly spaced indices for the later GENRAY comparison; no reference solver execution or accuracy result]{.claim}[C-278](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-278){.cid .st-measured}:
equally spaced state indices including both endpoints, independent of guard
outcome or surrogate error. Equilibrium, profile conversion, launch settings,
executable and resource bounds still need a concrete GENRAY package.

The first frozen package omitted dataset provenance sidecars. Its proof stages
failed during loading; the successful EC recordings were retained and reused.
A corrected package binds those sidecars and exercises all actual relocated
loaders before proof execution. Independent audits check the saved bounds,
feature reconstruction, inference outputs, raw guard masks, complete local
boxes, boundary reasons, process results and reference selection. Focused
validation is [70 focused checks pass normally and with Tier B disabled; lint, formatting and typing of all 92 source modules pass]{.claim}[C-277](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-277){.cid .st-measured}; it does not claim a fresh full-suite run.

## EC–GENRAY reference comparison {#ec-genray-reference-comparison}

The EC reference package is [forty decks bound to the unchanged selection, exact model and traces, frozen source, equilibrium, executable and runtime; eight workers with a thirty-minute hard limit]{.claim}[C-279](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-279){.cid .st-measured}. The implementation lives in
`tkit.verify.ec_reference`; entry 84 is the narrative account.
State selection is inherited without alteration from
the evenly spaced indices in the retained traces. The preparer checks model
and metadata hashes, feature names and dimensions, and exact state, time,
launch and guard identities. It independently reconstructs each input from
the saved face profiles at the reference tabular radii. The recorded feature
vector supplies the deck: temperature converts from electron-volts to
kilo-electron-volts and density to the reference tabular units. Launcher
positions and angles keep their original convention.

The request binds rendered decks, all toolkit source, the reference template
and equilibrium, executable, resolved shared-library bytes and Python version.
The batch process imports the frozen source explicitly. Preflight rechecks
those identities from the actual execution path. Exclusive evidence paths and
a request-level consumed marker prevent accidental reruns, including attempts
with different output paths. Each case has a hard timeout and retains the
actual deck, native output, logs, status and checksums. An audit reconstructs
the comparison from these bytes without rerunning the reference solver.

The reference absorbed power is the sum of Landau and collisional electron
heating. The existing current label and sign convention are retained: multiply
the native total current by the sign of the equilibrium plasma-current and
magnetic-field product, so co-current is positive. Native totals are normalized
by the actual injected power to the model's reference injection. Compare with
the physically bounded ensemble outputs recorded before guard selection.

For prediction $p$ and reference $r$, the per-case error is
$|p-r|/|r|$, checked against the unchanged tolerance in [C-279](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-279). No flux or
current denominator floor is introduced. An exactly zero reference passes
only with an exactly zero prediction; the remaining zero-reference errors
are undefined and fail. The report retains every case and its power and
current error. It reports both all-selected and served-only conjunctions;
any missing or failed reference makes the overall comparison incomplete.
Rejected-state predictions are diagnostic and cannot establish accuracy of
the source actually used by TORAX.

[K-028](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/ceilings.qmd#k-028) still applies: the reference uses the existing fixed equilibrium, rather
than a sequence matched to the evolving TORAX geometry. Agreement in this
comparison would test the retained surrogate/reference convention on loop
states; it would not establish a reference-coupled trajectory or certify M4.
[OQ-42](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/decisions.qmd#oq-42) and the measured EC local-domain limitation remain unchanged. Focused
validation is [40 affected tests pass normally and with Tier B disabled; repository lint, formatting, typing of 93 modules and batch syntax pass]{.claim}[C-280](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-280){.cid .st-measured}.

The completed run and independent saved-output audit give [40/40 cases pass the unchanged 10% power and signed-current limits, including 31/31 served states; maximum current error 9.606% EL and 7.393% UL, maximum power error 0.07483% EL and 0.02599% UL]{.claim}[C-281](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-281){.cid .st-measured}.
Every preselected case has a successful reference and meets both criteria,
including the subset served by the actual guard. The independent audit reloads
the frozen model, recomputes its predictions and reconstructs guard decisions
before comparing native-total algebra against the report. Rejected predictions
remain separately identified. This completes the sampled V9 comparison under
the existing reference convention; it does not lift [K-028](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/ceilings.qmd#k-028) or the EC local-box
limitation, and the M4 certification review remains pending.


## Verified artifacts in the guards {#guard-artifacts}

V10 loads each verified model through its digest-checked manifest. The explicit box must match the loader's feature order and previous domain. File IO occurs on the host before tracing; only arrays enter the compiled guard. Available output certificates hold a separate input box and output interval per family. The predicate applies only when an input lies inside an exact certified input box, with inclusive endpoints. Outside every proof box, it adds no certificate-based rejection; the ordinary input and physical-output checks still apply.

The ordinary EC numerical guard margin cannot enlarge a proof box. Removing that expansion from the inherited draft leaves none of the retained EC states inside its exact proof boxes; the pedestal trajectory is covered ([all four verified input boxes match the previous loaders; 48 of 48 retained pedestal states keep identical predictions and decisions; none of the 57 EC states is inside the exact proof boxes, so no EC certificate-based output check applies there]{.claim}[C-284](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-284){.cid .st-measured}). Transport has no finite output certificate under [OQ-46](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/decisions.qmd#oq-46). [OQ-50](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/decisions.qmd#oq-50) adopts the fallback-rate thresholds as report-only alerts. Accepted-state rejection is not internal solver usage.

## Hybrid-only calibration for M5 {#hybrid-calibration}

[OQ-48](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/decisions.qmd#oq-48) keeps the model, splits, V7 and the failed pooled record fixed. It restricts calibration to served states of the new hybrid runs and reporting to the older hybrid test runs. A shared state belongs to the family only when every owner run belongs to it. Absolute residuals in signed-log space use the same finite-sample split-conformal rank. A separate frozen reverse audit calibrates on the older hybrid test states and reports on the new ones. Every output must reach the existing pooled reading bar in both directions ([hybrid calibration covers 0.914/0.915/0.904 of the older hybrid test states; the reverse audit covers 0.887/0.869/0.900; all exceed the fixed 0.85 pooled bar]{.claim}[C-285](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-285){.cid .st-measured}).

Leaving each new run out reports the run-to-run coverage spread; pooled success does not imply a run-level or simultaneous guarantee. M5 uses one coherent uniform discrepancy factor multiplying these marginal half-widths, an explicit prior assumption rather than a distribution inferred from conformal coverage. Its separate Bayesian audit uses one mean residual vector per run, the full empirical channel covariance and a uniform scalar prior. Conditional Metropolis moments are compared with the exact truncated-normal posterior ([four Metropolis chains give transport-error factor mean -0.01978, standard deviation 0.01992 and split R-hat 1.00266; exact conditional moments are -0.02033 and 0.01984]{.claim}[C-288](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-288){.cid .st-measured}). The other physical priors are not calibrated.


## Portable pipeline boundaries {#pipeline-closeout}

V5 reports and provenance sidecars are packaged byte-for-byte. Model/manifest/box binding remains checked at load time, including when a wheel loads an external verified model directory ([installed-wheel EC and pedestal loaders retain their output certificates with externally copied verified directories; unresolved transport bounds remain explicitly K-033]{.claim}[C-289](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-289){.cid .st-measured}). An existing malformed manifest fails closed rather than dropping certificate checks. The fallback monitor applies identical validation to explicit API thresholds and YAML configuration, so nonfinite values cannot be reported as within threshold.

The M5 selector derives its decision from primary and reverse coverage, checks the unchanged reading bar for every channel and binds all evidence to the exact model and manifest. Scientific failure selects the unchanged V7 fallback; missing or altered evidence raises an error. The completed study's widths remain identical ([all three selected hybrid half-widths are unchanged; both-direction coverage and exact model/manifest/evidence bindings are rechecked before a future run]{.claim}[C-290](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-290){.cid .st-measured}). These are execution-integrity checks, not additional physics certificates.

## Complete-box partition pilot {#partition-pilot}

The follow-up partitions each original transport box into a complete binary cover. Each leaf uses the existing analytic LP support bands, independently finite variable boxes and stationarity-corrected inequality duals. Unknown or timed-out optimization retains the independently valid inherited enclosure; a primal objective is never accepted as a bound. The union must cover every original input, and aggregation must retain every leaf.

The independent audit reconstructs the cover, source and model bindings, fresh exported predictions, original held-out physical predictions and JAX predictions at sampled extrema. Both physical enclosures remain unresolved ([both member-zero pilots retain overflowing physical enclosures despite complete input-box coverage; no sampled overflow witness was found, and all forty transport V5 results remain unresolved]{.claim}[C-293](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-293){.cid .st-preliminary}). No sampled overflow witness was found. This does not establish a domain-wide finite enclosure or show the real-valued network is infinite. The calculation uses float64 without directed IEEE rounding guarantees.

Retained solver counters motivate a separate scheduling diagnosis: final output objectives can be skipped after intermediate work consumes a shared clock. A new method must reserve final-objective time, retain corrected duals for independent replay and undergo review before execution. The unchanged all-member gate still requires both pilot members to pass before expansion. [K-033](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/ceilings.qmd#k-033), dependent transport V6, EC local-domain exclusions and the human certification gate remain open.

### Reserved final-objective result {#reserved-final-objectives}

The bounded follow-up gives each intermediate activation a separate clock and reserves a final clock after every output head contributes constraints. Deterministic activation ordering permits cross-process replay. Incremental artifacts retain sparse constraints, finite variable boxes, affine forms, signed objectives, usable inequality duals and explicit interval fallback for every skipped or unusable objective. The independent auditor reconstructs the original graph and activation constraints, then replays stationarity corrections rather than trusting solver objectives or producer summaries.

All final objectives run, but the independently audited physical enclosures remain nonfinite ([both full-box pilots retain nonfinite physical enclosures after all final objectives run; independent graph, constraint and corrected-dual replay passes, with no finite physical candidate]{.claim}[C-297](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-297){.cid .st-preliminary}). Intersecting with the inherited enclosure preserves its endpoints exactly. Large relaxation terms dominate the small residual corrections; final-objective starvation alone does not explain the remaining looseness. Neither an identical retry nor an ensemble sweep follows from this result. The full-box property, stored models, guards and human acceptance gate remain unchanged.
